A daredevil is a person who deliberately does extremely dangerous things — things that most people would never attempt because the risk of serious injury or death is very real. The single most important thing to understand is that a daredevil does this willingly. They see the danger clearly, they understand it fully, and they go ahead anyway.

Picture someone who jumps off a skyscraper in a wingsuit, walks a tightrope stretched between two mountain peaks, or performs a motorcycle stunt over a row of burning vehicles. These are classic daredevil acts. The common thread is always the same: the danger is physical, the stakes are life-and-death high, and the person has chosen to be there.

This physical dimension matters. A daredevil faces risk to their own body and their own life. This is different from someone who takes a financial gamble or makes a bold career decision. Those might be brave choices, but we would never call them "daredevil" acts.

Daredevils are usually drawn by the rush of adrenaline, the love of pushing human limits, the desire to impress an audience, or simply the joy of doing something almost no one else dares to do. For many, the danger itself is part of the appeal — it makes the experience feel electrifyingly alive.

Here is an important nuance: a daredevil is not necessarily careless. A professional stuntman may spend months carefully preparing before performing a death-defying act. What makes them a daredevil is not a lack of preparation — it is the fact that they willingly take on a level of physical risk that most people would walk away from without hesitation.
Is it a compliment or a criticism?

"Daredevil" can be used both admiringly and critically, depending on how the speaker feels about the behavior.

When used admiringly, it highlights the person's remarkable courage. "She's a true daredevil — she solo-climbed that sheer cliff without a rope" communicates awe and deep respect.

When used critically, it suggests the person is being reckless and irresponsible. "Don't be a daredevil — those waves will kill you" warns that the behavior is dangerously foolish.

The word lives in a fascinating space between courageous and reckless. It acknowledges that the person is fearless, while leaving open the question of whether that fearlessness is admirable or foolish. Which side it leans toward depends entirely on who is speaking and why.

"Evel Knievel was one of the most celebrated daredevils in history, known for jumping his motorcycle over rows of cars and buses in front of massive crowds."

"Only a daredevil would attempt to free-climb the outside of that building."

"The crowd held its breath as the daredevil prepared to leap from the burning platform."

"He was the neighborhood daredevil — always the first to jump from the highest rock into the river below."
How it differs from similar words

A risk-taker is a broader term. Anyone who accepts uncertainty — in business, relationships, or finances — can be called a risk-taker. A daredevil is specifically about physical danger to one's body.

A thrill-seeker describes someone who craves excitement and adventure. The focus is on their internal desire. "Daredevil" puts the focus on the actions they actually take — specifically, the dangerously bold things they do in the real world.

A reckless person acts without thinking — they rush headlong into danger carelessly and impulsively. A daredevil, by contrast, may be completely aware of the danger and may have thought it through at length — they simply choose to do it anyway. A daredevil can be calculated; a reckless person typically is not.

A stunt performer is a professional who does dangerous acts for film or entertainment as their job. A daredevil can certainly be a stunt performer, but "daredevil" is less about professional role and more about a personal quality — a spirit of radical fearlessness and daring that defines who someone is.
When "daredevil" describes a thing, not a person

You will also encounter "daredevil" placed before a noun to describe something as extremely bold and dangerous — for example, "a daredevil stunt," "a daredevil leap," or "daredevil behavior." In these cases, the word simply means characteristic of a daredevil — involving extreme physical risk executed with boldness and fearlessness. This is the adjective form of the word, grown directly from the same noun, and it carries the exact same spirit.
